title: Developer Experience Docs Playbook — SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, and Canonical Fixes
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs site operations, and canonical fixes for top support issues. The goal is consistent, discoverable docs that reduce time-to-first-success for developers and shrink the support surface for the platform.

Audience:
- Engineers (frontend, backend, ML/infra) writing integrations.
- Developer experience writers and SDK owners.
- Support and solutions engineering teams using canonical fixes.

Ownership and governance:
- Primary owner: DevEx engineering (doc owner contact: devex-team@redwood.example.com)
- Review cadence: major updates reviewed quarterly; security, embargoed changes reviewed by Security.
- Publishing flow: draft -> in_review -> published (see Release & Review Process section).

Doc types covered (and when to use):
1. SDK Guide: full reference for a language SDK (API surface, auth, error handling, advanced features).
2. Quickstart: 5–10 minute tutorial to call the API and get meaningful output.
3. Template: reusable repo/readme + sample code (boilerplate starter).
4. API Example: single-purpose snippet demonstrating a feature (streaming, function-calling, embeddings, reranking).
5. Docs Site Ops: procedures to publish, rollback, and maintain site navigation and search.
6. Canonical Fix: triaged resolution for a top support issue with root cause, fix, and suggested doc/SDK changes.

Conventions and style (SDK guides):
- Structure: Overview, Installation, Authentication, Quick Example, API Reference, Error Codes, Best Practices, Migration Notes, Change Log.
- Code: provide minimal but copy-pastable examples for vX.Y SDK versions. Each example must include a short explanation and expected output.
- Error handling: include code patterns for retry/backoff, idempotency, and safe fallbacks.
- Versioning: indicate the SDK semantic version and compatible platform API version at top of the doc.
- Example authentication snippet (Node):

```js
// install: npm install @redwood/inference
import Redwood from '@redwood/inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'rw-instruct-1', prompt: 'Translate to French: Hello' });
console.log(resp.text);
```

Quickstarts and templates (requirements and process):
- Every quickstart must:
  - Complete in <10 minutes on a fresh environment.
  - Include package.json / requirements.txt and a README with commands.
  - Use environment variables for keys (do not commit secrets).
- Templates must include a CITATION.md that lists which SDK versions, Node/Python versions were validated.

Template metadata table (required fields):
| field | required | example |
|---|---:|---|
| template_name | yes | quickstart-node-chat |
| language | yes | node |
| runtime_validated | yes | node 18, npm 9 |
| supported_sdk | yes | @redwood/inference v2.1.0 |
| estimated_time | yes | 7 minutes |

API examples (best practices):
- Keep examples focused: one concept per snippet (streaming, function-calling, embeddings).
- Include both sync and streaming variants where applicable.
- Provide a CLI curl example for every SDK example to allow quick validation without SDK install.
- Example curl for a streaming completion (simplified):

curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-1","input":"Summarize the following...","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example.com/v1/generate

Docs site operating procedures (publish/rollback/search):
1. Local preview: run `yarn docs:dev` and validate examples run (see test matrix).
2. Linting: run `yarn docs:lint` (checks code blocks, broken links, markdown frontmatter).
3. CI validation: PR must pass `docs-e2e` that boots sample quickstarts in ephemeral containers.
4. Publish: merge to main -> CI publishes to staging -> Docs owner performs smoke test (3 smoke tests: install, run quickstart, run one API curl).
5. Rollback: tag previous published build and revert site config; file an incident in the status page and notify #devex.

Top support issues and canonical fixes (process):
- Triage owner (level-1 support) creates an incident ticket, assigns to SDK owner if SDK bug suspected.
- Create a canonical-fix doc under this directory with: root cause, minimal repro, fix, tests added, SDK patch if required, docs changed.
- Once merged, add a short note to the published quickstart referencing the fix and migration steps.

Common canonical fixes (examples):
1. Auth failure on old SDKs: root cause - header name change. Fix - add compat layer in SDK; patch release 2.1.1. Docs: update migration FAQ and add a curl example that shows the correct header.
2. Streaming timeouts: root cause - incorrect default keepalive in nginx ingress for private deployments. Fix - update default ingress config (see table below) and add fallback example that disables streaming fallback to chunked responses.

Ingress keepalive recommendations (private deployments):
| component | recommended | previous default | impact |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| nginx.ingress.keepalive_timeout | 60s | 15s | prevents premature stream closures |
| loadbalancer.idle_timeout | 120s | 60s | reduces mid-request disconnects |

Release & Review Process (summary):
1. Create a documentation PR against the `devex/docs` branch.
2. Assign at least one DevEx reviewer + one SDK owner reviewer.
3. PR must include: updated examples tested locally, CI passing, and updated quickstart template metadata.
4. After approvals, merge to main. The docs CI publishes to staging automatically; perform smoke tests; promote to production after signoff.

Operational runbook (when docs break or examples fail in CI):
1. Identify failing quickstart or example.
2. If failure is due to an SDK regression, label the ticket `sdk-regression` and notify SDK oncall.
3. If failure is environmental (node/python version), update template metadata and create a compatibility note.
4. Publish a temporary banner on the docs site indicating affected content and ETA for fix.

Metrics and KPIs (track monthly):
- Time-to-first-success: median minutes for new users to run a quickstart. Target: <10 minutes.
- Number of support tickets referencing docs errors. Target: <= 4/month per major doc area.
- Quickstart CI pass rate. Target: >= 95%.

Appendix — Example canonical-fix checklist (for PR):
1. Issue ticket created and linked.
2. Repro steps included.
3. Minimal failing test added.
4. Fix implemented and unit/integration test added.
5. Docs updated (example and migration note).
6. Release notes entry added.

Related resources:

- Docs site repo: git@github.com:redwood-inference/docs-site.git
